question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

A person who collects and studies coins.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Numismatist.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Numismatist" means one who collects and studies coins, from Greek nomisma, meaning current coin. (सिक्कों का संग्रहकर्ता)
◦ Example: As a numismatist, she could identify the origin of a coin just by its markings.

 

• The suffix "-ist" denotes a person devoted to something; compare Philatelist (stamps) and Bibliophile (books).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 2: Philatelist (डाक टिकट संग्रहकर्ता): A person who collects postage stamps.

 

• Option 3: Bibliophile (पुस्तक प्रेमी): A person who loves and collects books.

 

• Option 4: Antiquarian (पुरावस्तु संग्रहकर्ता): A person who collects or studies ancient objects.

 

NOTE

 

• Other collector-type SSC words: Philatelist (stamps), Bibliophile (books), Antiquarian (antiques), Connoisseur (expert taste in fine arts, food or wine).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Philanthropist (परोपकारी): A person who works for others' welfare

2. Xenophobia (विदेशियों का भय): Fear or hatred of foreigners

3. Claustrophobia (बंद स्थान का भय): Fear of confined spaces

4. Laconic (संक्षिप्त): Using very few words

5. Ephemeral (अल्पकालिक): Lasting for a very short time

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

A person who believes people are motivated purely by self-interest and doubts their sincerity.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Cynic.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Cynic" means one who doubts others' sincerity or motives, from Greek kynikos (dog-like), referring to the Cynic school of philosophers who scorned convention. (निंदक)
◦ Example: Being a cynic, he assumed the charity drive was just for publicity.

 

• Do not confuse Cynic (doubts sincerity/motives) with Skeptic (doubts truth/facts) or Pessimist (expects bad outcomes) — each targets a different object of doubt.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: Skeptic (संशयवादी): A person who doubts the truth of claims or accepted beliefs.

 

• Option 3: Misanthrope (मानवद्वेषी): A person who dislikes or distrusts humankind in general.

 

• Option 4: Pessimist (निराशावादी): A person who always expects the worst outcome.

 

NOTE

 

• Commonly confused attitude words in SSC: Skeptic (doubts truth of claims), Misanthrope (hates mankind), Pessimist (expects the worst), Optimist (expects the best).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Altruist (परोपकारी व्यक्ति): A person who selflessly cares for others

2. Stoic (अविचल): A person who endures pain without showing feelings

3. Hedonist (सुखवादी): A person who believes pleasure is the most important thing

4. Recluse (एकांतवासी): A person who lives in seclusion

5. Prodigy (अद्भुत प्रतिभाशाली व्यक्ति): A person with exceptional talent from a young age

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

An abnormal fear of open or crowded public spaces.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Agoraphobia.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Agoraphobia" means fear of open or crowded places, from Greek agora (open assembly place) and phobos (fear). (खुले स्थानों का भय)
◦ Example: His agoraphobia made it difficult for him to visit crowded markets.

 

• The suffix "-phobia" always means an irrational fear; the first part names what is feared, e.g. claustro- (enclosed spaces) versus agora- (open spaces).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: Claustrophobia (बंद स्थान का भय): Fear of confined or enclosed spaces.

 

• Option 2: Acrophobia (ऊँचाई का भय): Fear of heights.

 

• Option 3: Xenophobia (विदेशियों का भय): Fear or hatred of foreigners.

 

NOTE

 

• Other phobia words for SSC: Claustrophobia (enclosed spaces), Acrophobia (heights), Xenophobia (foreigners), Nyctophobia (darkness), Hydrophobia (water).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Nyctophobia (अंधेरे का भय): Fear of darkness

2. Arachnophobia (मकड़ियों का भय): Fear of spiders

3. Insomnia (अनिद्रा): Inability to sleep

4. Somnambulist (नींद में चलने वाला व्यक्ति): A person who walks while asleep

5. Gourmet (भोजन विशेषज्ञ): A connoisseur of good food

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

A person who knows and can use several languages.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Polyglot.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Polyglot" means a person who knows many languages, from Greek polys (many) and glotta (tongue/language). (बहुभाषी)
◦ Example: Being a polyglot, she conducted the interview fluently in five different languages.

 

• Do not confuse Polyglot (knows many languages) with Linguist (studies language scientifically) — a linguist need not speak many languages.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 2: Linguist (भाषाविज्ञानी): A person who studies the scientific structure of language(s).

 

• Option 3: Interpreter (दुभाषिया): A person who translates spoken words orally from one language to another.

 

• Option 4: Translator (अनुवादक): A person who converts written text from one language to another.

 

NOTE

 

• Related language-based SSC words: Linguist (studies language), Interpreter (translates speech), Translator (translates text), Monoglot (knows only one language).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Monoglot (एकभाषी): A person who knows only one language

2. Verbose (शब्दाडंबरपूर्ण): Using more words than needed

3. Garrulous (बातूनी): Excessively talkative

4. Taciturn (मितभाषी): Habitually silent or reserved in speech

5. Loquacious (वाचाल): Very talkative

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

Not having life; lacking the qualities associated with living things.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Inanimate.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Inanimate" means not alive; lacking life, from Latin in- (not) and anima (breath, soul, life). (निर्जीव)
◦ Example: A rock is an inanimate object with no biological processes.

 

• Do not confuse Inanimate (never alive, e.g. a stone) with Comatose (alive but unconscious) or Extinct (was once alive but has died out as a species).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 2: Inert (निष्क्रिय): Lacking the ability or tendency to move or react; chemically inactive.

 

• Option 3: Comatose (प्रगाढ़ बेहोशी में): In a prolonged state of deep unconsciousness, though still alive.

 

• Option 4: Extinct (विलुप्त): No longer in existence; died out completely.

 

NOTE

 

• Contrast words: Animate (having life), Inert (inactive/unreactive), Extinct (no longer existing), Dormant (temporarily inactive but capable of reviving).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Dormant (निष्क्रिय/सुषुप्त): Temporarily inactive but capable of becoming active

2. Animate (सजीव): Having life

3. Sentient (संवेदनशील): Able to perceive or feel things

4. Latent (अप्रकट): Present but not yet active or visible

5. Perennial (चिरस्थायी): Lasting for a very long time or all year round

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

A form of government in which power is held by a small group of people.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Oligarchy.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Oligarchy" means government run by a small group of people, from Greek oligos (few) and arkhein (to rule). (कुलीनतंत्र)
◦ Example: Critics claimed the country was really an oligarchy controlled by a handful of business families.

 

• The suffix "-archy" relates to rule/government; compare Oligarchy (rule by few) with Monarchy (rule by one) and Anarchy (absence of government).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: Monarchy (राजतंत्र): Government ruled by a single king or queen.

 

• Option 2: Autocracy (निरंकुश शासन): Government ruled by one person with absolute, unchecked power.

 

• Option 3: Plutocracy (धनिकतंत्र): Government controlled by the wealthy class.

 

NOTE

 

• Other government-type SSC words: Monarchy (one ruler), Autocracy (absolute one-person rule), Plutocracy (rule by the rich), Theocracy (rule by religious authority), Democracy (rule by the people), Anarchy (no government/lawlessness).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Theocracy (धर्मतंत्र): Government ruled by religious authority

2. Anarchy (अराजकता): Absence of government or law

3. Bureaucrat (नौकरशाह): An official who works in a government department

4. Despot (निरंकुश शासक): A ruler with absolute power, often cruel

5. Plebeian (सामान्यजन): A common person of ordinary rank

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

Lacking imagination or excitement; dull and ordinary.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Prosaic.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Prosaic" means dull, unimaginative, and ordinary, from Latin prosa (straightforward discourse), as opposed to poetry. (नीरस)
◦ Example: The lecture was so prosaic that half the students dozed off.

 

• Prosaic originally contrasted 'prose' with 'poetry', and came to mean plain, dull, and unimaginative in a wider sense.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: Verbose (शब्दाडंबरपूर्ण): Using or containing more words than necessary.

 

• Option 3: Eloquent (वाक्पटु): Fluent and persuasive in speaking or writing.

 

• Option 4: Lucid (स्पष्ट): Expressed clearly and easily understood.

 

NOTE

 

• Contrast with: Eloquent (fluent, persuasive speech), Lucid (clear, easily understood), Verbose (wordy), and Vivid (producing powerful, clear images in the mind) — the opposite quality to prosaic.

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Vivid (जीवंत/स्पष्ट): Producing powerful, clear images in the mind

2. Mundane (सांसारिक): Dull, ordinary, everyday

3. Pedantic (पंडिताऊ): Overly concerned with minor details or rules

4. Erudite (विद्वान): Having great knowledge gained from study

5. Succinct (संक्षिप्त): Expressed clearly in few words

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

A sentimental longing for the past, especially a happy time in one's own life.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Nostalgia.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Nostalgia" means a longing or sentimental feeling for the past, from Greek nostos (return home) and algos (pain). (अतीत की याद)
◦ Example: The old song filled her with nostalgia for her college days.

 

• Nostalgia specifically involves a longing for the past, unlike Reminiscence, which is simply the act of recalling memories without necessarily implying longing.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: Reminiscence (स्मृति/यादों का जिक्र): The act or process of recalling past experiences or events.

 

• Option 3: Melancholy (विषाद): A deep, thoughtful sadness without an obvious cause.

 

• Option 4: Sentiment (भावना): A general feeling or emotional attitude.

 

NOTE

 

• Related feeling-words: Reminiscence (recalling memories), Melancholy (pensive sadness), Wistfulness (a vague or regretful longing), Homesickness (longing for home while away).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Homesickness (घर की याद): A feeling of longing for one's home

2. Wistful (उदासी और लालसा से भरा): Having a feeling of vague or regretful longing

3. Sentimental (भावुक): Prone to emotional feelings rather than reason

4. Poignant (मार्मिक): Evoking a keen sense of sadness

5. Elegy (शोक गीत): A poem of serious reflection, typically a lament for the dead

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

The method and practice of teaching, especially as an academic subject.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Pedagogy.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Pedagogy" means the art or method of teaching, from Greek paidagogos, a slave who escorted children to school (pais = child, agogos = leader). (शिक्षाशास्त्र)
◦ Example: The training programme focused on modern pedagogy for primary school teachers.

 

• Do not confuse Pedagogy (teaching children/students generally) with Andragogy (teaching methods specifically for adults).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: Curriculum (पाठ्यक्रम): The subjects comprising a course of study in a school or college.

 

• Option 2: Andragogy (प्रौढ़ शिक्षण विधि): The method and practice of teaching adult learners.

 

• Option 4: Didactics (शिक्षण सिद्धांत): The theory and principles of teaching methods.

 

NOTE

 

• Related education words: Curriculum (course of study), Andragogy (adult teaching methods), Didactics (theory of teaching), Pedagogue (a teacher, sometimes in a strict or pedantic sense).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Pedagogue (शिक्षक): A teacher, especially a strict or formal one

2. Alumnus (पूर्व छात्र): A former student of a school or college

3. Truant (विद्यालय से अनुपस्थित रहने वाला व्यक्ति): A student who stays away from school without permission

4. Autodidact (स्वशिक्षित व्यक्ति): A self-taught person

5. Mentor (मार्गदर्शक): An experienced and trusted advisor

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

A formal public speech or piece of writing that praises someone highly.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Panegyric.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Panegyric" means a formal speech of high praise, from Greek panegyrikos, a speech given at a general public assembly. (प्रशंसा भाषण)
◦ Example: The retiring professor was honoured with a panegyric by his former students.

 

• Do not confuse Panegyric (formal praise of a living or general subject) with Eulogy (praise specifically for someone who has died).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: Eulogy (श्रद्धांजलि भाषण (मृतक हेतु)): A speech praising someone who has recently died.

 

• Option 2: Elegy (शोक गीत): A mournful poem, typically written as a lament for the dead.

 

• Option 3: Tribute (श्रद्धांजलि): An act, statement, or gift intended to show gratitude or respect.

 

NOTE

 

• Related speech/writing types: Eulogy (praise for the dead), Elegy (mournful poem), Tirade (a long angry speech of criticism), Diatribe (a forceful verbal attack).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Tirade (फटकार भरा लंबा भाषण): A long, angry speech of criticism

2. Diatribe (कटु आलोचना): A forceful verbal attack against someone

3. Rhetoric (वाक्पटुता): The art of effective or persuasive speaking

4. Soliloquy (स्वगत भाषण): A speech a character gives to themselves, especially on stage

5. Anecdote (किस्सा): A short, interesting story about a real incident

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

A person who has, or professes to have, a special appreciation of beauty and art.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Aesthete.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Aesthete" means a lover and admirer of beauty and art, from Greek aisthetes, one who perceives, related to aisthesis (perception, sensation). (सौंदर्यप्रेमी)
◦ Example: As a true aesthete, he could spend hours admiring a single painting.

 

• Aesthete is the direct opposite of Philistine — one loves art and beauty, the other is indifferent or hostile to it.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 2: Connoisseur (पारखी): A person with expert knowledge and judgement in art, food, or wine.

 

• Option 3: Philistine (कला-विरोधी/असंस्कृत व्यक्ति): A person who is indifferent or hostile to art, culture, and beauty.

 

• Option 4: Virtuoso (कला में निपुण व्यक्ति): A person highly skilled in an art, especially music.

 

NOTE

 

• Related art-appreciation words: Connoisseur (expert judge), Virtuoso (highly skilled performer), Philistine (indifferent to art), Dilettante (a person with a superficial interest in an art).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Dilettante (शौकिया कला-प्रेमी): A person with a superficial or amateur interest in an art

2. Prodigious (अद्भुत): Remarkably great in extent or size

3. Novice (नौसिखिया): A person new to and inexperienced in a field

4. Veteran (अनुभवी व्यक्ति): A person with long experience in a field

5. Maestro (संगीत गुरु): A distinguished musician, especially a conductor

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

Of little value or importance; not significant.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Trivial.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Trivial" means of little importance or value, from Latin trivialis, found everywhere, hence commonplace (trivium, a place where three roads meet). (तुच्छ)
◦ Example: They argued over a trivial matter that hardly mattered in the end.

 

• Trivial means unimportant, while Superfluous means unnecessary/excess — a thing can be important yet superfluous if there is too much of it, so the two are not synonyms.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: Paramount (सर्वोपरि): More important than anything else; supreme.

 

• Option 2: Pivotal (महत्वपूर्ण/निर्णायक): Of crucial importance to a situation or plan.

 

• Option 3: Superfluous (अनावश्यक): Unnecessary, especially through being more than enough.

 

NOTE

 

• Antonyms and near-words: Paramount (supremely important), Pivotal (crucial), Significant (important), Petty (small and unimportant, often of behaviour), Trifling (of very little value).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Petty (छोटा/तुच्छ): Small and unimportant, often used of behaviour

2. Trifling (नगण्य): Of very little value or importance

3. Significant (महत्वपूर्ण): Important enough to be worthy of attention

4. Redundant (अनावश्यक): Not needed; superfluous

5. Indispensable (अपरिहार्य): Absolutely necessary

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

Occurring at irregular intervals; not constant or frequent.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Sporadic.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Sporadic" means occurring irregularly or occasionally, from Greek sporadikos, scattered, from speirein (to sow). (अनियमित)
◦ Example: There were only sporadic showers throughout the otherwise dry month.

 

• Do not confuse Sporadic (irregular, occasional) with Periodic (regular, at fixed intervals) — they describe opposite patterns of occurrence.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 2: Perpetual (चिरस्थायी/सतत): Never ending or changing; continuing forever.

 

• Option 3: Incessant (अविरत): Continuing without pause or interruption.

 

• Option 4: Periodic (आवधिक): Occurring at regular intervals.

 

NOTE

 

• Related frequency words: Periodic (regular intervals), Incessant (without pause), Perpetual (never ending), Intermittent (starting and stopping repeatedly, similar to sporadic).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Intermittent (रुक-रुक कर होने वाला): Occurring at irregular intervals; not continuous

2. Chronic (दीर्घकालिक): Persisting for a long time

3. Fleeting (क्षणभंगुर): Lasting for a very short time

4. Recurrent (पुनरावर्ती): Occurring often or repeatedly

5. Transient (अस्थायी/क्षणिक): Not permanent; passing through or lasting only briefly

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

A person thought to be guilty of a crime or offence.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Suspect.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Suspect" means a person believed to have committed a crime, from Latin suspicere, to look up at, hence to mistrust. (संदिग्ध)
◦ Example: The police detained the suspect for questioning about the burglary.

 

• A suspect is only believed or thought to be guilty, whereas a culprit is one who is actually established to be guilty — the two are not interchangeable.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: Culprit (अपराधी): A person who is guilty of a specified crime or offence.

 

• Option 2: Accomplice (सहअपराधी): A person who helps another commit a crime.

 

• Option 3: Witness (गवाह): A person who sees an event, such as a crime or accident, take place.

 

NOTE

 

• Related legal/crime words: Culprit (proven guilty party), Accomplice (helper in crime), Witness (one who observes an event), Perpetrator (the person who actually commits a crime), Informer (one who gives information about a crime to authorities).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Perpetrator (अपराध करने वाला): The person who actually commits a crime

2. Informer (मुखबिर): A person who gives secret information to the police or authorities

3. Alibi (अन्यत्र उपस्थिति का प्रमाण): A claim of being elsewhere when a crime occurred

4. Vigilante (स्वयंभू न्यायकर्ता): A person who takes law enforcement into their own hands

5. Fugitive (फरार अपराधी): A person who is running away, especially from the law

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

Spoken or done without any prior preparation.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Extempore.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Extempore" means spoken or done without preparation, from Latin ex tempore, literally out of the time (of the moment). (बिना तैयारी के)
◦ Example: She delivered an impressive extempore speech on environmental issues.

 

• Extempore and Impromptu are close in meaning, but extempore usually refers to speeches given without preparation, while impromptu covers any spontaneous, unplanned act.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: Verbatim (शब्दशः): In exactly the same words as were used originally; word for word.

 

• Option 3: Rehearsed (पूर्वाभ्यास किया हुआ): Practised or prepared in advance.

 

• Option 4: Impromptu (अचानक/बिना योजना के): Done on the spur of the moment without any plan.

 

NOTE

 

• Related speech/preparation words: Impromptu (unplanned action), Verbatim (word for word), Rehearsed (practised beforehand), Ad-lib (to speak without preparation, especially to fill time).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Adlib (बिना तैयारी के बोलना): To speak or perform without preparation

2. Candid (स्पष्टवादी): Truthful and straightforward

3. Articulate (सुव्यक्त): Able to express oneself clearly

4. Coherent (सुसंगत): Logical and consistent; easy to follow

5. Fluent (धाराप्रवाह): Able to speak or write smoothly and easily

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

A statement that seems self-contradictory or absurd but may actually be true.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Paradox.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Paradox" means a seemingly contradictory statement that is actually true, from Greek paradoxon, contrary to expectation (para = beyond, doxa = opinion). (विरोधाभास)
◦ Example: It is a paradox that the more you learn, the more you realise you don't know.

 

• Do not confuse Paradox (a self-contradictory statement that can still be true) with Oxymoron (just two contradictory words placed together, like jumbo shrimp).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: Irony (विडंबना): A situation or outcome that is the opposite of what is expected, often humorous.

 

• Option 2: Anomaly (असंगति/अपवाद): Something that deviates from the normal or expected pattern.

 

• Option 4: Oxymoron (विरोधाभासी शब्दालंकार): A figure of speech combining contradictory terms, e.g. deafening silence.

 

NOTE

 

• Related logic/language words: Irony (contrary-to-expectation situation), Anomaly (deviation from the norm), Oxymoron (contradictory word pair), Fallacy (a mistaken belief based on unsound reasoning).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Fallacy (भ्रांति): A mistaken belief based on unsound reasoning

2. Ambiguous (अस्पष्ट): Open to more than one interpretation

3. Enigma (पहेली): Something puzzling or mysterious

4. Conundrum (जटिल समस्या): A confusing and difficult problem or question

5. Cryptic (गूढ़): Having a meaning that is mysterious or obscure

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

A calm, graceful, and self-assured manner or bearing.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Poise.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Poise" means calm, graceful, and dignified behaviour, from Old French pois/peser, to weigh, suggesting balance. (संतुलन/गरिमा)
◦ Example: She handled the difficult questions at the press conference with remarkable poise.

 

• Poise combines physical grace with emotional balance, while Composure refers mainly to emotional calmness under pressure — poise has a slightly broader, more graceful connotation.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: Composure (धैर्य/आत्मसंयम): The state of being calm and in control of one's emotions.

 

• Option 3: Arrogance (अहंकार): An offensive display of superiority or self-importance.

 

• Option 4: Nonchalance (उदासीनता/लापरवाही): A casual lack of concern; indifference.

 

NOTE

 

• Related demeanour words: Composure (calmness under pressure), Equanimity (mental calmness in difficulty), Nonchalance (casual indifference), Arrogance (offensive superiority, an antonym in tone).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Equanimity (समभाव): Mental calmness and composure, especially in a difficult situation

2. Aplomb (आत्मविश्वास): Self-confidence or assurance, especially in a demanding situation

3. Decorum (शिष्टाचार): Behaviour in keeping with good taste and propriety

4. Grace (शालीनता): Elegance and beauty of movement or form

5. Dignity (गरिमा): A calm, serious manner deserving of respect

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

A published notice announcing a person's death, often with a brief biography.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Obituary.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Obituary" means a published announcement of someone's death, from Latin obitus, death, from obire, to die. (मृत्यु लेख)
◦ Example: The newspaper carried a lengthy obituary for the celebrated scientist.

 

• Do not confuse Obituary (a published death notice with biography) with Epitaph (words carved on a tombstone) or Eulogy (a spoken tribute at a funeral).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: Epitaph (समाधि-लेख): Words inscribed on a tombstone in memory of the dead person.

 

• Option 2: Eulogy (श्रद्धांजलि भाषण): A speech praising someone who has recently died.

 

• Option 3: Memoir (आत्मकथात्मक संस्मरण): A written account of a person's own memories and experiences.

 

NOTE

 

• Related death/memorial words: Epitaph (tombstone inscription), Eulogy (funeral speech of praise), Elegy (mournful poem for the dead), Requiem (a mass or musical composition for the dead).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Requiem (शोक गीत/मृतक संस्कार गीत): A mass or musical composition performed in honour of the dead

2. Memorial (स्मारक): Something built or done to remember a person or event

3. Legacy (विरासत): Money or property left to someone in a will; a lasting influence

4. Posthumous (मरणोपरांत): Happening or awarded after a person's death

5. Cenotaph (स्मृति-स्तंभ): A monument to someone buried elsewhere, especially war dead

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

Belonging or seeming to belong to a period other than the one in which it exists.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Anachronistic.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Anachronistic" means out of its proper time period, from Greek ana (against) and khronos (time). (कालविरुद्ध)
◦ Example: Showing a character using a smartphone in a film set in the 1800s would be anachronistic.

 

• Anachronistic specifically means placed in the wrong time period, while Obsolete simply means no longer in use — a thing can be obsolete without being anachronistic in a narrative sense.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: Obsolete (अप्रचलित): No longer produced or used; out of date.

 

• Option 2: Archaic (पुरातन/प्राचीन): Very old or old-fashioned, no longer in ordinary use.

 

• Option 4: Contemporary (समकालीन): Belonging to or occurring in the present time period.

 

NOTE

 

• Related time-based words: Obsolete (no longer used), Archaic (very old-fashioned), Contemporary (of the present time), Antiquated (outdated, old-fashioned, similar to obsolete).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Antiquated (पुराने ढंग का): Outdated or old-fashioned

2. Modern (आधुनिक): Relating to the present or recent times

3. Timeless (कालातीत): Not affected by the passage of time

4. Vintage (पुराने समय का उत्कृष्ट): Denoting something from the past of high quality

5. Retrospective (पूर्वव्यापी): Looking back on or dealing with past events

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

Fond of the company of others; sociable.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Gregarious.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Gregarious" means sociable; fond of the company of others, from Latin grex/gregis (flock, herd). (मिलनसार)
◦ Example: He is a gregarious person who loves attending parties and meeting new people.

 

• Gregarious is the opposite of Reclusive/Aloof — one thrives in company, the others avoid or keep distance from it.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 2: Reclusive (एकांतप्रिय): Preferring to avoid the company of other people.

 

• Option 3: Amiable (मित्रवत/सौम्य): Friendly and pleasant in manner.

 

• Option 4: Aloof (उदासीन/अलग-थलग): Distant and reserved; not friendly or forthcoming.

 

NOTE

 

• Related personality words: Reclusive (avoids company), Aloof (distant, reserved), Amiable (friendly), Sociable (enjoys being with others, a close synonym), Introvert (a person who prefers solitary activities).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Sociable (मिलनसार): Willing and inclined to talk and engage with others

2. Introvert (अंतर्मुखी व्यक्ति): A person who prefers solitary activities to social ones

3. Extrovert (बहिर्मुखी व्यक्ति): An outgoing, socially confident person

4. Amicable (मैत्रीपूर्ण): Friendly and without disagreement, usually of relations

5. Congenial (अनुकूल/सुखद): Pleasant or agreeable because suited to one's taste

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

Extremely large, ugly, or frightening; also, shockingly cruel or wrong.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Monstrous.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Monstrous" means extremely large, cruel, or shocking, from Latin monstrum, an omen or a monster. (भयानक)
◦ Example: The dictator committed monstrous crimes against his own people.

 

• Monstrous covers both huge/frightening size and extreme cruelty, so context decides which sense is meant, unlike Gigantic, which refers only to size.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: Gigantic (विशालकाय): Extremely large in size.

 

• Option 2: Benevolent (दयालु/परोपकारी): Well meaning and kindly; generous.

 

• Option 4: Grotesque (विकृत/भद्दा): Comically or repulsively distorted in appearance.

 

NOTE

 

• Related words: Gigantic (huge in size only), Grotesque (distorted appearance), Barbaric (extremely cruel and violent), Colossal (immense in size).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Barbaric (बर्बर): Extremely cruel and violent

2. Colossal (विशाल): Extremely large in size or extent

3. Ferocious (क्रूर/उग्र): Savagely fierce or cruel

4. Ruthless (निर्दयी): Having no pity or compassion

5. Diminutive (छोटा/नन्हा): Extremely or unusually small

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

A person, traditionally a singer or minstrel, who composes and recites poetry.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Bard.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Bard" means a poet, traditionally one who sings verses, from Celtic bard, a tribal poet-singer, now used as an epithet for Shakespeare. (कवि)
◦ Example: Shakespeare is often referred to simply as the Bard of Avon.

 

• Bard traditionally implies a poet who also sings or performs verses aloud, close to a Minstrel, but a minstrel is more specifically a travelling musician-entertainer.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: Orator (वक्ता): A skilled and eloquent public speaker.

 

• Option 3: Minstrel (गायक-गीतकार (मध्यकालीन)): A medieval singer or musician who performed songs and stories.

 

• Option 4: Laureate (पुरस्कृत कवि): A poet honoured for outstanding work, especially by an official title.

 

NOTE

 

• Related literary/performance words: Minstrel (travelling musician-poet), Laureate (honoured poet), Orator (public speaker), Rhapsodist (one who recites epic poetry, historically).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Rhapsodist (महाकाव्य-गायक): One who recites epic poetry, especially in ancient Greece

2. Chronicler (वृत्तांत-लेखक): A person who writes a record of historical events in order

3. Raconteur (किस्सागो): A person who tells stories and anecdotes skilfully

4. Satirist (व्यंग्यकार): A writer who uses satire to expose vices or follies

5. Lyricist (गीतकार): A person who writes the words for songs

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

A group of wild animals, especially wolves, that live and hunt together.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Pack.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Pack" means a group of wild animals such as wolves, from Middle English/Middle Dutch pak, a bundle, later extended to a group of animals. (भेड़ियों का समूह)
◦ Example: A pack of wolves hunted the deer across the snowy plain.

 

• SSC exams frequently test collective nouns for animal groups — memorise them by animal: Pack (wolves/hounds), Herd (cattle), Flock (sheep/birds), Swarm (bees/insects).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: Herd (पशुओं का झुंड (गाय/हिरण आदि)): A group of grazing animals such as cattle or deer.

 

• Option 2: Flock (पक्षियों/भेड़ों का झुंड): A group of birds, or a group of sheep or goats.

 

• Option 4: Swarm (कीड़ों का झुंड): A large group of insects, especially bees, moving together.

 

NOTE

 

• Common collective nouns: Herd (cattle, elephants), Flock (sheep, birds), Swarm (bees, locusts), Pride (lions), Shoal/School (fish), Gaggle (geese).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Pride (शेरों का समूह): A group of lions

2. Shoal (मछलियों का समूह): A large group of fish swimming together

3. Gaggle (हंसों का झुंड): A group of geese

4. Litter (एक साथ जन्मे पशु-शावकों का समूह): A group of young animals born at one time to the same mother

5. Colony (जीवों की बस्ती): A group of the same kind of animals or plants living together

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

An intense fear or anxiety about speaking in front of an audience.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Glossophobia.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Glossophobia" means fear of public speaking, from Greek glossa (tongue/language) and phobos (fear). (सार्वजनिक बोलने का भय)
◦ Example: His glossophobia made him break into a sweat before every classroom presentation.

 

• The suffix "-phobia" denotes irrational fear; glosso- relates to language/speech, so glossophobia is fear tied specifically to speaking, not writing or listening.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: Claustrophobia (बंद स्थान का भय): Fear of confined or enclosed spaces.

 

• Option 2: Xenophobia (विदेशियों का भय): Fear or hatred of foreigners.

 

• Option 4: Acrophobia (ऊँचाई का भय): Fear of heights.

 

NOTE

 

• Other phobia words for SSC: Claustrophobia (enclosed spaces), Xenophobia (foreigners), Acrophobia (heights), Agoraphobia (open/crowded places), Nyctophobia (darkness).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Reticent (अल्पभाषी): Not revealing one's thoughts readily; reserved in speech

2. Diffident (संकोची): Modest or shy because of a lack of self-confidence

3. Timid (भीरु): Showing a lack of courage or confidence

4. Assertive (दृढ़): Confident and direct in stating one's views

5. Bashful (शर्मीला): Shy or self-conscious

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

A person who deliberately chooses to remain unmarried, often for religious reasons.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Celibate.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Celibate" means one who chooses to remain unmarried, from Latin caelebs, unmarried, single. (अविवाहित)
◦ Example: He remained celibate throughout his life, devoting himself entirely to religious service.

 

• Celibate implies a deliberate, often vow-based choice to stay unmarried (frequently for religious reasons), unlike Bachelor, which simply describes any unmarried man regardless of reason.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 2: Bachelor (अविवाहित पुरुष): An unmarried man.

 

• Option 3: Spinster (अविवाहित/कुंवारी स्त्री (विशेषतः वृद्ध)): An unmarried woman, especially an older one.

 

• Option 4: Widower (विधुर): A man whose wife has died and who has not remarried.

 

NOTE

 

• Related marital-status words: Bachelor (unmarried man), Spinster (unmarried woman, older), Widower/Widow (spouse died), Divorcee (formerly married, now legally separated).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Divorcee (तलाकशुदा व्यक्ति): A person who has legally ended their marriage

2. Widow (विधवा): A woman whose husband has died and who has not remarried

3. Misogamist (विवाह-द्वेषी): A person who hates marriage

4. Monogamy (एकविवाह): The practice of having only one spouse at a time

5. Polygamy (बहुविवाह): The practice of having more than one spouse at the same time
